scope: Deterministic bounded-work contracts plus sequential local Debug real-Parquet controls during concurrent native/E2E validation. No measured end-to-end latency or real-cloud throughput improvement is established.

baseline_binary_source.qualification: previous tuple-recipe executable, before reader protocol 86

conclusions.answers: All 48 samples match independently derived expected application IDs and the comparison also verifies normalized full answers, including totals and continuation presence. All cases retain 21 decorations.
conclusions.timing: Warm medians are 28–30 ms versus baseline 24–26 ms; restarted complete-tuple medians are 161–171 ms versus 188–189 ms, while wide/public-ID controls are 219–222 ms versus 192–198 ms. Concurrent load and sequential runs prevent attribution; no latency win is claimed.
conclusions.ownership: An initial candidate failed on a wide primary tie because deferred lineage borrowed temporary admission arrays. The final executable deeply owns compact descriptors, has no acquired snapshot pointer, and passes all four cases. Regression frees admission storage before point and inverse reads and covers allocation failures.

paged_lineage.scope: authenticated metadata read charges, not measured network transfer

capture_ordering.scope: hashed identity plus ordered captured rows; each missing block decoded once per fragment; no measured old-executable decode ratio

oracle.derivation: Same independently validated eight-file fixture and expected application-ID arrays as native-routing-refresh-v3-observation.json. This plan removes relational indexes and declares revision ASC, id ASC, _id ASC to exercise native segment admission. It does not derive expected answers from the candidate.

comparison.environment_scope: same declared platform and collector; sequential runs are observational, not randomized paired trials

baseline.input_identity_contract: identity checked around launches/measurements and content verified before completion
